newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds vulnerable on break below 108-30.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds vulnerable on break below 108-30.

text.p: U.S. T-bond futures may suffer a slight setback on Thursday, particularly if they break below 108-30, technical analysts said.
But various support levels in the 108 handle mean it was unlikely to see a dramatic slide, they added.

"T-bonds will likely trade sideways to a little down, with the fall becoming temporarily more exagerated if we take out the 109-03 low yesterday and then 108-30," said Adrian Sells, director at Crane Investment Analysis.
"But we probably won't get anywhere much lower than 108-16," he said, adding he expected the market to bottom out around that level.
By 0941 GMT, June T-bonds were unchanged at 109-09.
T-bonds have been trapped in sideways trade since the beginning of the month, consistently failing to break above the 110-16 level.
Sells put closer resistance at 109-20,22, an area of intra-day congestion on Wednesday.
Analysts said the May 2 high at 110-10 and the May 13 high at 110-22 still looked hard to beat medium term.
Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank said the T-bond should head lower towards the key 108-30 level, for a break to 108-12 and lower.

"The latter zone is expected to offer decent support, but there is some scope for accelerated losses to the April 11 low of 106-12," he said in a note. He added that move was not really favoured but should be watched closely.
"Dips will be attractive further out with the medium term view still focused on range trading in a 6.75 percent to 7.25 percent zone for the long bond," said Celaya.
By 1009 GMT, the September Eurodollar contract was down 0.005 at 93.955.
